import pandas as pd

# Read the input Eurostat raw data
input_file = 'outputs/t02_eurostat_raw.csv'
output_file = 'outputs/t11_city_indicator_matrix.csv'

# Read the CSV
df = pd.read_csv(input_file)

# Get unique indicator_ids from the input data
indicator_ids = sorted(df['indicator_id'].unique())

# Pivot to wide format: one row per city_id/year, columns for each indicator
# Using pivot_table with fill_value='' for missing values
df_wide = df.pivot_table(
    index=['city_id', 'city_name', 'year'],
    columns='indicator_id',
    values='value',
    aggfunc='first',
    fill_value=''
)

# Reset index to make city_id, city_name, year regular columns
df_wide = df_wide.reset_index()

# Write to CSV with RFC 4180 compliance
# pandas to_csv handles quoting of fields with commas, quotes, or newlines automatically
df_wide.to_csv(output_file, index=False)

print(f"Created {output_file} with {len(df_wide)} rows and {len(indicator_ids) + 3} columns")
</solution_file>
